title: $L^q$ contractivity of the one-bit noise operator
statement:
Let $q \ge 1$ and let $\rho$ be a real number with $0 \le \rho \le 1$. Then for every Boolean function $g \colon \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ on a single bit, the noise operator $T_\rho$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl(\E\!\left[\,\abs{T_\rho g}^{\,q}\,\right]\bigr)^{1/q}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\!\left[\,\abs{g}^{\,q}\,\right]\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^1$.
hypotheses_covered: g is a Boolean function on one bit
replaced:
For $q \ge 1$, $0 \le \rho \le 1$ and $g : \mathrm{BoolCube}\,1 \to \bbr$,
\[
  \bigl(\E[\abs{T_\rho g}^q]\bigr)^{1/q} \;\le\; \bigl(\E[\abs{g}^q]\bigr)^{1/q},
\]
i.e.\ $T_\rho$ is a contraction in $L^q$ on one bit.
